drawings.description: en marge gauche, sous la note oblique, un petit schéma de relations : $F' \ll F$ au-dessus de $G' \ll G$, un signe d'inclusion vertical ($\cup$) sous $F'$ et un autre sous $F$.
drawings.notes: F' << F above G' << G, a vertical inclusion sign (cup) under F' and another under F, as on the page. The F' is written over another letter (it looks overwritten); read F' as in the transcription. Left out: the fragments of the oblique marginal note above and to the left (text, not part of the schema). Nothing struck. Method: a relation diagram of formulas, which the transcription skill would set as text (tikz-cd); since it stands only as a \drawing mark, it is set here as a TikZ layout of the formula: every symbol is a LaTeX text node at its place on the page, the arrows are drawn between them. Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again.

drawings.description: moitié gauche, premier schéma, entièrement biffé (surchargé et barré de traits obliques) : \ill{} $\to F' \subset \overline{F}' \xrightarrow{\sim} F$ au-dessus de $\overline{G}' \xrightarrow{\sim} \overline{G}' \subset \overline{G} \simeq G$, avec des inclusions verticales.
drawings.notes: Wholly struck on the page: overwritten and crossed by long oblique strokes. The redraw is empty. What can be seen under the strokes: a scribbled symbol, -> F' (included in) F-bar' ~-> F on the top row, G-bar' ~-> G-bar' (included in) G-bar ~ G on the bottom row, with vertical inclusions, as the transcription says. Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again. 2026-11-13, Claude Opus 5.5, issue 147, overlay check on the 250 ppi scan at 400 dpi: the whole schema is overwritten and crossed by long oblique strokes. By the editor's rule for wholly crossed-out figures (#146, 156-6 04-2: what lies under the strike is drawn, in ink, without the strike) this one should be set as a diagram; it is left empty in this pass because its first node is an illegible scribble and the places of the vertical inclusions under the strokes could not be read with certainty at this resolution. Still partial for that reason.

drawings.description: moitié gauche, deuxième schéma : $\Phi \subset \overline{F}'' \xrightarrow{\sim} F' \subset \overline{F}' \xrightarrow{\sim} F$ au-dessus de $\overline{G}'' \xrightarrow{\sim} G' \subset \overline{G} \xrightarrow{\sim} G$, avec des flèches verticales descendantes.
drawings.kind: relation diagram (subdivisions ~-> and inclusions), set as a tikz-cd diagram
drawings.notes: Set as a tikz-cd diagram, as the editor asks for arrow diagrams (#146): top row Phi (included in) F-bar' ≃ F' (hooked inclusion) F-vec ~-> F; bottom row, from under F-bar': G-bar' ~-> G' (hooked inclusion) G-bar ~-> G; between the rows, under F-bar', F', F-vec and F, the small vertical cup he writes for an inclusion, set as a cup between the nodes. The layout is canonical and keeps the shape of the scheme, not its geometry (not overlaid). Read on the page: the first top and bottom nodes carry one prime each (F-bar', G-bar'; Michel's check, #142); the third top node is an F under a bar corrected by a small arrow, set as F-vec (machine pass of 2026-11-12; the cube at the foot of the page has the same chain); the sign between F-bar' and F' is « ≃ » with no arrowhead; the inclusions F' to F-vec and G' to G-bar are hooked strokes with no head. Left out as struck: the scribbled insertion above F' (an F-bar with a ~ and an arrow, struck through). Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128) as a TikZ layout of the formula; revised 2026-11-11 (#142) and 2026-11-12. 2026-11-13, Claude Opus 5.5, issue 147: the earlier layout was overlaid on the 250 ppi scan at 400 dpi (labels within about one unit, but the vertical relations drawn as long arrows where the page has small cups) and is replaced by the tikz-cd setting. Not compiled (no TeX in the session). Disagreement with the transcription: between F-bar' and F' the page has « ≃ » without arrowhead, and the vertical relations are cups, not « flèches descendantes ».
drawings.disagreement: Michel, #142: the primes of the first top and bottom nodes are one each, F-bar prime and G-bar prime, as on the crop. The third top node has no prime: it is an F-bar with an arrow added, i.e. F-vec as in the cube below; the transcription has F-bar prime.

drawings.kind: relation diagram (subdivisions ~-> and inclusions), set as a tikz-cd diagram
drawings.notes: Set as a tikz-cd diagram, as the editor asks for arrow diagrams (#146): top row F-bar' (hooked inclusion) F-tilde ~-> F-vec ~-> F; bottom row, from under F-tilde: G-tilde ~-> G-bar ~-> G; between the rows, under F-tilde, F-vec and F, the small vertical cup he writes for an inclusion, set as a cup between the nodes. Read on the page: the middle bottom node is G-bar (the mark above its bar is the cup; machine pass of 2026-11-12, and the cube below has the same row); under F the page has the same cup as under the other two, not an arrow. Left out: the top of the large arc that encloses the fourth schema, which passes under this one. Nothing struck. Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128) as a TikZ layout of the formula. 2026-11-13, Claude Opus 5.5, issue 147: the earlier layout was overlaid on the 250 ppi scan at 400 dpi (labels within about one to two units, the cups drawn as arrows) and is replaced by the tikz-cd setting. Not compiled (no TeX in the session).

drawings.description: moitié gauche, en bas, entouré d'un grand arc, un cube de relations : en haut $\Phi \subset \overline{F}'$, $\widetilde{F}$, $\vec{F}$, $F$ ; au milieu $F'$ ; en bas $\overline{G}'$, $\widetilde{G}$, $\overline{G}$, $G$, $G'$ ; des flèches marquées $\simeq$ (subdivisions) et des flèches verticales.
drawings.notes: Large arrow diagram, drawn as the skill prescribes for these: nodes placed as on the page, the principal arrows between them, labels as the transcription reads them. Top face: Phi (included in) -> F-bar'; F-bar' to F-tilde by a curved inclusion arrow; F-tilde ~-> F-vec ~-> F. Middle: F', reached from F-bar' by a ~-> arrow and joined to F-vec by a curved inclusion arrow; a vertical stroke from F-tilde down to F'. Bottom face: G-bar', G-tilde ~-> G-bar ~-> G, and G' reached from G-bar' by a ~-> arrow, with a short inclusion hook from G' towards G-bar and from G-bar' towards G-tilde. Vertical strokes: F-bar' down to G-bar', F' down to G-tilde, F-vec down to G-bar, F down to G, and a long vertical from F' down past G-tilde to G'. The large arc that encloses it is drawn. Left out: the heavy hatched scribble at the top (struck), and the F' at the far left joined to it by a double stroke (read as part of that struck insertion; doubtful). Arrowheads and hooks are approximate. Method: a relation diagram of formulas, which the transcription skill would set as text (tikz-cd); since it stands only as a \drawing mark, it is set here as a TikZ layout of the formula: every symbol is a LaTeX text node at its place on the page, the arrows are drawn between them. Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again. Question settled by a machine pass on the facsimile, 2026-11-12 (maths): the F' at the far left is crossed by the same double stroke that leads into the hatched scribble, and no arrow of the cube reaches it; the cube needs one F' only, the middle one, which carries the arrows from F-bar' and to F-vec. The far-left F' is struck with the insertion and stays left out. Not checked by a reader. 2026-11-13, Claude Opus 5.5, issue 147, overlay check: not compiled (no TeX in the session); the TikZ was rasterised by a local interpreter and laid over the 250 ppi scan at 400 dpi. Nothing changed. The nodes, the arrows and the large arc lie within about one to two units of their ink; the vertical relations are drawn as strokes where the page has small cups and hooks, and the arrowheads are approximate. Still partial: a large arrow diagram, which the editor asks to be set in LaTeX (the cube of 156-6 04-2, #146); the kinds of its arrows (hooks, cups, ≃ with or without head) need a closer reading before it is set as tikz-cd.

drawings.description: en marge droite, un petit schéma : $F$ et $F'$ sur une ligne, reliés par un signe de subdivision surchargé et barré ; sous $F$, un signe d'inclusion vertical ($\cup$), puis $G$ ; sous $F'$, un trait vertical en pointillés, puis $G'$ ; entre $G$ et $G'$, des points.
drawings.notes: F and F' on a line; under F a vertical inclusion sign (cup), then G; under F' a dotted vertical stroke ending in a small blot, then G'; two dots between G and G'. Left out as struck: the subdivision sign between F and F', overwritten and struck, and the long oblique stroke that crosses it (one of the strokes striking the paragraph). The transcription's description matches. Method: a relation diagram of formulas, which the transcription skill would set as text (tikz-cd); since it stands only as a \drawing mark, it is set here as a TikZ layout of the formula: every symbol is a LaTeX text node at its place on the page, the arrows are drawn between them. Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again. Question settled by a machine pass on the facsimile, 2026-11-12 (page): at 700 dpi the sign between F and F' is made of heavy curved strokes written over one another, a curly « precedes or equals » with its point towards F, and is not scribbled out; the only stroke across it is one of the two long thin oblique lines that strike the whole paragraph, which are left out everywhere. The sign is now drawn, and the dots between G and G' are three, as on the page. Not checked by a reader.
drawings.disagreement: The sign between F and F' is overwritten, not struck: the only stroke across it is one of the long obliques that strike the paragraph (the transcription has « surchargé et barré »).

drawings.description: au-dessus des deux schémas, une première esquisse du même carré, entièrement biffée de longs traits obliques ; on y devine $G$, $H'$, $H$, $G'$, des signes $\geq$ verticaux et un $F$ repassé.
drawings.notes: Wholly struck on the page: a first sketch of the square, crossed by long oblique strokes, with overwritten signs. The redraw is empty. What can be seen under the strokes: G, H', H, a vertical >=, H, G', G, vertical >= signs and an F written over. Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again. 2026-11-13, Claude Opus 5.5, issue 147, overlay check on the 250 ppi scan at 400 dpi: the sketch is crossed by long oblique strokes and overwritten. By the editor's rule for wholly crossed-out figures (#146, 156-6 04-2) what lies under the strike would be drawn; here it cannot be: the letters G, H', H, G' and the ≥ signs are seen, but not how they are arranged into the square (the fair version is the next schema). The redraw stays empty; still partial for that reason.
